value.rationale: The number and exact boundaries of secondary peaks in an earthquake cluster's expected rate is a motivated qualitative discriminant of delayed triggering. A rigorous first-echo branching threshold, full mode-count law and exponentially accumulating higher-echo thresholds distinguish multi-stage triggering from single-stage or two-stage kernels. Extremely near-critical higher echoes are scientifically interpretable but potentially hard to observe; no claim about observed seismicity is made.
